- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward more aggressively.
- Model frequently overcorrects after sharp price spikes — reduce forecast by 5–10% in the immediate next period.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, model tends to overpredict; if below, underpredict — adjust toward historical volatility range.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model often lags by 1–2 periods in reaction to sentiment shifts — delay adjustment by 1–2 days if sentiment changes sharply.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction — align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
- Overshoot after bullish sentiment: if sentiment >0.67 and price spikes, forecast should be capped at 10–15% below peak to avoid overcorrection.
